content: The title of the classification page should be formatted as (Disease name) classification, with only the first letter of the title capitalized. The purpose of this page is to provide detailed information on any condition-specific classification schema that may exist. If the classification schema is minimal, it can be included within the pathophysiology microchapter rather than having its own page. For an example of a microchapter on classification, refer to the provided link. When creating microchapter pages that link to the main page, include the {{CMG}} template, your name template, and the microchapter navigation template at the top of the edit box. For instance, if a sentence mentions anterior spinal artery syndrome, the link should direct to anterior spinal artery syndrome rather than generic terms like anterior, artery, or syndrome. For further guidance on creating links, refer to the provided link. It is important to distinguish between classification and the natural history of a disease. For example, the progression of primary, secondary, and tertiary syphilis falls under the natural history of the disease, as it represents the chronological progression of the same illness. In contrast, hepatic encephalopathy and hypoxic encephalopathy represent classifications of encephalopathy. Follow the specified format and capitalization rules as outlined in the template. Additionally, include the disease name in the first sentence of every subsection. The overview section should begin with the disease name in the first sentence. This section aims to summarize the page in a few sentences, typically outlining the categories by which the disease is classified. For an example, refer to the provided link. In the classification section, list the categories under which the disease can be classified and provide a brief description of each. Diseases may be classified at a pathological level based on their manifestations or appearance. If the disease can be classified under multiple categories, consider creating subheadings titled Classification Based On [specific criteria]. For an example of a page with multiple classification schemes, refer to the provided link. For malignant diseases with staging systems, use the specified template when adding content to the classification page. Include a table that outlines the different stages and provides a definition for each stage. The table can be as detailed or as simple as the staging system requires. If a malignant disease lacks a staging system, explicitly state this on the classification page by writing, There is currently no staging system for [disease name]. It is crucial to note that staging and grading of malignant diseases are not synonymous and should not be used interchangeably. Staging describes the spread and extent of the disease, typically based on clinical features and imaging findings. For example, the TNM (Tumor-Nodes-Metastasis) system is a common staging system. The disease stage should be included in the Stage microchapter for that disease. Grading, on the other hand, describes the pathological features of cancer cells, such as differentiation or growth rate, based on histopathological analysis. For instance, prostate cancers are graded using the Gleason grading system. If there is no classification system for a disease, state, There is no established system for the classification of [disease name]. If a classification system exists, use the following templates: 1. For diseases with multiple subgroups: [Disease name] may be classified according to [criteria] into [subtypes/groups]: [list of subtypes/groups]. 2. For diseases with multiple established classification methods: [Disease name] may be classified into [subtypes] based on [criteria]. 3. For diseases classified as acute or chronic: Based on the duration of symptoms, [disease name] may be classified as either acute or chronic. 4. For malignant diseases with staging systems: According to the [staging system], there are [number] stages of [disease name] based on [criteria]. Each stage is assigned a [letter/number] that designates [specific features]. 5. If the staging system does not conform to the above template, state, The staging of [disease name] is based on [criteria], and elaborate further. 6. If there is no staging system for a malignant disease, state, There is no established system for the staging of [disease name].
